experience.blurb: Four client projects in two years, shipping hybrid apps to both stores from one codebase.
story: I joined my first job with a college friend and that is where I learned to code and build software. I was lucky to have two capable mentors, Indranil Mondal and Raju Bera, who taught me how to turn an idea into actual lines of code.

I started building mobile apps, worked with Ionic and React Native, and held an iOS device for the first time. I also used DSA to solve a graph problem and built a recursive file explorer. Getting it to work felt amazing. For the first time, I felt I could build almost anything.

experience.blurb: Led frontend for enterprise security products, then took on more of the backend as I went.
story: Four years on enterprise security software: Netskope, Swift Security, Zuellig Pharma. Around 500 tenants and 10k+ users, with hotfixes that had to land inside the SLA window along with whatever database migration came with them.

The move off Angular onto React ran module by module behind a micro-frontend setup, so nothing got rewritten twice. Test coverage went from 35% to 90% across several teams and production issues dropped by about 70%.

experience.blurb: I spend most of my time coding, solving problems, and arguing with juniors about why not every problem needs a new library installed or a new AI tool.
story: As a Tech Lead, I spend more time designing systems and figuring out how everything fits together then write code when everyone sleeps. I prompt my colleagues, they prompt systems, and then I review the generated mess.

Somehow the planning keeps getting longer while the coding keeps getting shorter. Then at 2 AM, I'm arguing with a machine that writes the code itself, wondering if I’m still the engineer or just the guy keeping the chaos together.
